content.text: The failure is configuration-level, not a malformed source file: the hook includes `rotation_controls.js`, while `.clang-format` explicitly declares itself C++-only. I’m checking the hook’s intended file scope and whether one shared style can safely cover both the C shim and JavaScript.

const r = await tools.exec_command({"cmd":"git log -8 --oneline -- .clang-format .pre-commit-config.yaml src/postgkyl/render/rotation_controls.js && git log -p -3 -- .clang-format .pre-commit-config.yaml && sed -n '1,260p' src/postgkyl/render/rotation_controls.js && git diff -- .pre-commit-config.yaml .clang-format src/postgkyl/render/rotation_controls.js src/postgkyl/gpython/csrc/_gpythonmodule.c","workdir":"/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl","yield_time_ms":10000,"max_output_tokens":30000});
text(r.output);

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/.pre-commit-config.yaml
@@
   - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/mirrors-clang-format
     rev: v22.1.3
     hooks:
       - id: clang-format
+        types_or: [c, c++]
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

content.text: The hook is now explicitly limited to C/C++, matching the repository’s formatter contract (“YAPF for Python, clang-format for C”). The local environment does not have `pre-commit` installed, so I’m validating the exact file selection and formatter output with the available tooling, then I’ll run the relevant tests/config checks.

The override therefore removes only the accidental JavaScript input; it does not weaken formatting coverage for any intended source.
